blogs.title: Chopta in Winter: The Complete Snow Trek Guide (2026)
blogs.author: Vikram Rawat
blogs.excerpt: Everything you need to know before your first snow trek — best dates, what to wear at −8°C, and how to catch the Chandrashila sunrise.
content: Chopta is often called the Mini Switzerland of India, and in winter it earns the name. From December to February the meadows around Chopta and the trail to Tungnath disappear under a thick blanket of snow.

The best window for a snow trek is late December to mid-February. Earlier, you may get patchy snow; later, the upper trail can become icy. Start the summit push by 4 AM to catch sunrise from Chandrashila.

Layering is everything: a thermal base, a fleece mid-layer and a down or padded jacket on top. Add woollen socks, waterproof gloves and a balaclava. We provide microspikes and gaiters on all winter batches.
Finally — go slow. The altitude gain from Chopta (2,680 m) to Chandrashila (4,000 m) is significant. Hydrate, eat well and listen to your trip captain.

blogs.title: Kedarnath Yatra for First-Timers: Registration, Trek & Tips
blogs.author: Neha Joshi
blogs.excerpt: How to register, which route to take, when to book a helicopter and what to pack for the 16 km trek to Baba Kedar.
content: Registration for the Char Dham yatra is mandatory and free on the official Uttarakhand tourism portal. Do it at least two weeks before your trip.
The trek from Gaurikund to Kedarnath is 16 km with a steady climb. Most people take 6–8 hours. Ponies, palkis and helicopter services are available if you need them.
Carry warm clothes even in summer — nights at Kedarnath drop close to zero. A good pair of shoes and a rain jacket are non-negotiable.

blogs.title: 7 Weekend Getaways from Dehradun Under ₹5,000
blogs.author: Aditya Thapa
blogs.excerpt: Rishikesh rafting, Kanatal camping, Chakrata waterfalls and more — quick escapes you can plan on a Thursday night.
content: Dehradun is the perfect base for weekend escapes. Within 3–4 hours you can be rafting in Rishikesh, camping in Kanatal or chasing waterfalls in Chakrata.

Our favourites: Rishikesh (rafting + camping), Kanatal (Surkanda Devi + camping), Chakrata (Tiger Falls), Mussoorie (Lal Tibba sunrise), Dhanaulti (eco parks), Lansdowne (quiet walks) and Tehri (water sports).
Most of these can be done for under ₹5,000 per person including stay, food and transport when you travel in a group.

blogs.title: The Only Himalayan Trek Packing List You Need
blogs.author: Vikram Rawat
blogs.excerpt: A tried-and-tested checklist from 200+ treks — what to carry, what to rent and what to leave at home.
content: Pack light, pack smart. A 40–50L backpack is enough for most 4–6 day treks.
Essentials: trekking shoes, 3 layers of warm clothing, rain gear, headlamp, water bottle, sunscreen, personal medicines and a photo ID.
Leave behind: jeans (they never dry), heavy cotton, and more than one pair of casual shoes.

blogs.title: Spiti vs Ladakh: Which Himalayan Road Trip Is Right for You?
blogs.author: Neha Joshi
blogs.excerpt: Both are high-altitude cold deserts, but the experience is very different. Here is how to choose.
content: Ladakh is bigger, busier and better connected. Spiti is rawer, quieter and more village-centric.
If you have 10+ days and want iconic lakes and passes, go Ladakh. If you want homestays, monasteries and fewer tourists in 7–8 days, pick Spiti.

blogs.title: Harshil: Uttarakhand's Best-Kept Secret
blogs.author: Aditya Thapa
blogs.excerpt: Apple orchards, deodar forests and the Bhagirathi — why Harshil should be on your list before it gets crowded.
content: Tucked away on the road to Gangotri, Harshil is a village of wooden houses, apple orchards and endless deodar forests.
Visit in October for apple season or in December for snow. Stay at least two nights to explore Dharali, Mukhba and the Sattal meadows.
